title: Preferences: Support configuring debounce timers
description:
Make it possible for users to configure
the debounce timers.
Fixes #17867

notes.body:
added 364 commits
  • 78028766...1229b0a9 - 363 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 2b59345b - Preferences: Support configuring debounce timers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9106/diffs?diff_id=576357519&start_sha=78028766777ea185ae5ce09c326e218de7c9c955)
Was 200 too short of a default?

Yes, as commented below (https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9106#note_1244661166), I used 400 this time because 1000 felt very long, and when I searched online, it seemed like more typical debounce timers were 250-500ms. (e.g., https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42361485/how-long-should-you-debounce-text-input ).
Ok
Again, you've changed this to 400 by default..

Yes, as the other one also changed from 200 to 400.
I used 400 this time because 1000 felt very long, and when I searched online, it seemed like more typical debounce timers were 250-500ms. (e.g., https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42361485/how-long-should-you-debounce-text-input ).
Find by me

This works fine for me (I am lucky in that the I don't seem to need a high value).

The one thing that confused me was that I had to dismiss the overall preferences dialog with OK before a new value would take effect.  I guess there aren't many preference settings that also affect the preferences dialog itself...

Also, is the expectation that this preference would be used elsewhere in the code (e.g. auto-complete / colouring for display filters) ?  I wouldn't have known this was for advanced preference search unless I saw it in the sources.  The long text for the preference suggests it may be used wherever it is needed...

I think the key for debouncing is that it should be used when processing the user input would normally take a significant amount of CPU time.

As such, if filtering a UI element would anyways take under 100 ms, debouncing probably isn't necessary. However, if it takes more than, say, 1000 ms, debouncing would be recommended. Anywhere in between is a judgement call.

While the CPU time needed for an action will depend on the system's processor, the default value was chosen so that even if debouncing isn't needed, the debouncing shouldn't negatively impact the user.
